paper_id: Ji et al. - 2017 - On Improving Wireless Channel Utilization A Collision Tolerance-Based Approach
title: On Improving Wireless Channel Utilization: A Collision Tolerance-based Approach
motivation: Collision avoidance protocols waste channel capacity through backoff overhead and idle slots, especially in dense networks with intensive traffic.
problem_framing: Formulate channel utilization as an optimization problem over transmission probability p, where collision tolerance enables concurrent successful transmissions.
key_insight: Capture effect at the physical layer allows successful reception of a stronger signal amid collisions, enabling tolerance instead of avoidance.
method_signature: Coco protocol: sender alignment via ACK-triggered SFD interrupts, plus feedback control of transmission probability p for optimal concurrency.
evaluation_criteria: Channel utilization improvement (≥20%), protocol lightness, fairness index, convergence speed measured in diverse topologies.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Average reception ratio drops to near zero when >7 senders transmit; concurrency must be strictly limited (≤4 optimal).
evidence_for_taste: collision avoidance comes at the cost of miscellaneous overhead
an inherent conflict between collision avoidance and channel utilization
tolerate or even allow collisions instead of simply avoiding them
controlling the transmission concurrency is relatively effective and easy to implement
thinking_moves: 从协议层传统假设反推物理层能力被低估
将最优化理论模型作为算法收敛的目标标准
通过实验观察发现并发数阈值(≤4)的硬约束
把时序对齐问题转化为SFD中断触发的同步机制
